world.headline: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills at least 132 in western Colombia
world.body: The quake struck Chocó Department on 10 August, 20 km from San José del Palmar, with at least 132 dead and 570 injured according to the Colombian Association of Capital Cities. Cali, Manizales, Pereira and Quibdó sustained heavy damage — the pediatric and neonatal wings of a Cali hospital collapsed. The government has declared a national disaster and deployed soldiers to the region.

world.headline: OpenAI says internal "Astra" model cracked ten open math problems
world.body: OpenAI published formal Lean proofs on GitHub for ten unsolved problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, including a construction proving the existence of non-sofic groups and new sphere-packing bounds. Fields Medallist Timothy Gowers said he would recommend one of the proofs to a top journal without hesitation — a rare outside endorsement in a field usually sceptical of machine-generated results.

world.headline: Frontier model releases now face a US national-security review gate
world.body: The Commerce Department has set capability thresholds above which new models require government review before launch, catching releases such as GPT-5.6 and Claude Fable 5. It lands alongside the EU AI Act entering full, strict enforcement — the two regimes together now define the compliance floor for anyone shipping a frontier model globally.

world.headline: Inference prices collapse again as ChatGPT nears a billion weekly users
world.body: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna pricing by 80% to $0.20 per million input tokens, while ChatGPT reached roughly one billion weekly active users. Google and Anthropic simultaneously widened access to task-running agents, with Anthropic pushing a one-million-token context window — the competitive front has shifted from raw benchmarks to cost-per-task.

world.headline: Seventy ships still trapped in the Gulf; Iran and Oman weigh tolled passage
world.body: Nearly six months into the Iran–US conflict, at least 70 vessels remain stalled in the Persian Gulf after the ceasefire collapsed, with attacks intensifying across the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Tehran and Muscat are reportedly negotiating an arrangement to ease transit in exchange for maritime service fees paid to a newly created corporation — converting what was free navigation into a tolled corridor.

world.headline: Turkey–Pakistan–Saudi defence pact signals a realigning Middle East
world.body: A new mutual defence arrangement between Ankara, Islamabad and Riyadh cuts across the region's traditional alignments. Analysts read it as a hedge against both Iranian escalation and uncertain US security guarantees — and it carries direct implications for New Delhi given Pakistan's involvement.

world.headline: Ukraine runs out of Patriot interceptors while pushing deeper into Russia
world.body: Kyiv has exhausted its Patriot stocks even as it expands operations across the Russian border. Elsewhere on this week's watchlist: renewed fighting in Ethiopia's Tigray region risks fusing two large-scale Horn of Africa conflicts, Iraq has issued an ultimatum on militia disarmament, and the DRC Ebola outbreak continues.

world.headline: Markets price a Fed cut that Powell has not promised
world.body: The Nasdaq rose 1.30% and the S&P 500 added 0.62% to 7,758, tying its 52-week high, while gold vaulted 2.11% to $4,342 an ounce and silver jumped nearly 3%. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.651% and the dollar index fell below 100 to 99.539 — a full dovish repricing built on a consensus the Fed itself has yet to confirm. This week's US CPI print is the test.

world.headline: This year's El Niño is on track to be the strongest ever recorded
world.body: Central equatorial Pacific temperatures have sat at record levels for over two months, with effects expected to peak late this year and into next. 2026 is currently tracking 1.58°C above the pre-industrial average; June was the second-warmest on record globally, with more than 24 countries setting national heat records.

world.headline: Total solar eclipse crosses Europe tomorrow; NASA buys Voyager 2 more time
world.body: A total eclipse darkens parts of Europe on 12 August, with Spain offering the best viewing. Separately, NASA engineers executed an operation nicknamed the "Big Bang" — simultaneously shutting down power-hungry hardware aboard Voyager 2 to extend a mission now approaching fifty years since launch.

india.headline: US judge dismisses all criminal fraud charges against Gautam Adani
india.body: District Judge Nicholas Garaufis dismissed the case against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain with prejudice on 10 August, finalising an $18 million SEC settlement. The DOJ had alleged a scheme to pay over $250 million in bribes for solar contracts. Garaufis sharply criticised the department's "terse, bland and conclusory" motion, and declined for now to drop bribery and obstruction charges against five co-defendants.

india.headline: RBI holds repo at 5.25%, lifts FY27 growth forecast to 6.7%
india.body: The Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously on 5 August to hold rates and keep a neutral stance, while cutting the inflation outlook to 5.0% and raising the GDP forecast on stronger-than-expected Q1 manufacturing and domestic demand. Governor Malhotra described the RBI as "neither dovish nor hawkish," citing Middle East tensions as a key uncertainty. Next meeting: 5–7 October.

india.headline: Jharkhand exam row escalates: BJP bandh today, ED opens probe
india.body: Student protests over the state examination controversy have widened, with the BJP calling a bandh for 11 August and the Enforcement Directorate launching an investigation. Chief Minister Hemant Soren said the government has heard the students and will address their demands "with seriousness and sensitivity."

india.headline: Monsoon session opens amid opposition protests over Ram Mandir donations
india.body: Both Houses convened as opposition MPs demonstrated inside the Parliament premises over the temple donation row, with NDA and opposition members coming face to face during rival protests. The session also saw the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill debated, with MPs flagging data security and digital inclusion concerns.

india.headline: Sensex slips 320 points in early trade; ED freezes 182 accounts in chit-fund case
india.body: The Sensex fell 320.14 points to 78,204.40 and the Nifty dropped 94.35 to 24,490.85 at the open, diverging from the global risk-on mood. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate froze 182 bank accounts and seized ₹1 crore in cash in connection with a ₹2,000 crore chit-fund scam.

india.headline: PM E-DRIVE extended to March 2028 with a ₹11,900 crore outlay
india.body: The Centre has pushed the electric mobility incentive scheme out by two years, giving manufacturers and charging-infrastructure operators a longer planning runway. The extension keeps demand-side subsidies in place through the next two fiscal years rather than letting them lapse mid-cycle.

india.headline: Semicon 2.0 commits ₹1.275 trillion across the chip value chain
india.body: Launched 15 July, the second phase spans design, fabrication, display manufacturing, advanced packaging, equipment, specialty materials, R&D and talent development — deliberately broader than fab subsidies alone. Domestic chip startups raised $92 million in the first five months of 2026, and Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said India is on course to be a top-four semiconductor manufacturing nation by 2035.

india.headline: ISRO sets a four-year deadline for home-grown space-grade chips
india.body: The agency plans to manufacture its own semiconductors domestically within four years, ending a dependence on imported space-grade chips that has driven delays and cost overruns on satellite and launch programmes. It is the clearest link yet between the space programme and the national chip push.

india.headline: Uttarakhand bridge washed away as an erratic monsoon runs a 16% deficit
india.body: Heavy rainfall in the Niti Valley region raised river levels and swept away a major bridge. Nationally the season has swung between dry spells and violent downpours since onset on 4 June, leaving more than half of districts rain-deficient while floods and landslides hit the west, northwest and northeast. Scientists link the volatility to El Niño, western disturbances and warming.

india.headline: Women's Asia Cup looms in Dubai; Ganguly reports death threat to police
india.body: The Women's Asia Cup runs 28 August to 13 September in Dubai, with India–Pakistan on 5 September; the men next appear at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, where cricket starts 24 September. Off the field, former BCCI president Sourav Ganguly and his wife Dona have lodged a complaint with Kolkata Police after receiving a death-threat letter.
